title: Human Tasks Canvas
description: Tracks offline human tasks (interviews, observations, outreach). Created by /handoff, consumed by /log-evidence and session-start.sh. Bridges agent-executable and human-executable work.

touch_log.description: Chronological log of exchanges on this task's channel. Formalised in v0.68.0: it existed as an undocumented convention surviving only on additionalProperties, so nothing could safely read it. `direction` is what makes a task's state legible - without it an inbound and an outbound are indistinguishable, and a task where the CONTACT is waiting on YOU looks identical to one where you are waiting on them.

direction.description: Who moved. `outbound` = you contacted them. `inbound` = they contacted you. `bidirectional` = a two-way exchange captured as one entry (no reply is owed - it completed). `internal` = an observation or note with NO contact (a metric reading, a status note); these are skipped entirely when locating the last contact, so an internal note logged on top of an inbound does not conceal the owed reply. Keep the value bare - annotations belong in `purpose`, since a qualified value like 'outbound (founder-sent)' defeats the machine read this field exists for. NOT required: pre-v0.68.0 logs have none and must keep validating on upgrade; entries without it are unevaluable rather than invalid.

purpose.description: What was sent, received, or observed.

closure_reason.description: Why this was closed. Must name what happened, not how long it has been.

reopen_trigger.description: What would make this closure wrong, stated concretely enough to be checked by someone who was not there. This is the field that turns a stale closure into a detectable one.

horizon.description: When this task's outcome should be read, ISO-8601. USED IN PRACTICE AND UNDECLARED UNTIL v0.97.0 — 22 occurrences in the dogfood canvas, and canvas-health check 8c(b) reads it to decide whether an open task is genuinely stale or legitimately waiting. A field a shipped check depends on must be declared: undeclared means unvalidated, so a typo like `horizion` degrades the check silently instead of failing.
